title: NumPy (Numerical Computing)
description: Vectorized arrays, multi-dimensional array manipulation, fancy indexing, broadcasting rules, and numerical computing tricks.

lessons.title: NumPy Array Creation & Multidimensional Shapes
lessons.concept_markdown:
NumPy (`numpy`) is the foundational package for scientific computing in Python. It provides the N-dimensional array object (`ndarray`), which stores homogeneous data in contiguous memory blocks, enabling vectorized calculations without slow Python `for` loops.
- `np.array(list, dtype=...)`: Creates an ndarray
- `np.arange(start, stop, step)`: Array of evenly spaced values
- `np.zeros(shape)`, `np.ones(shape)`: Initialized constant arrays
- `arr.reshape(rows, cols)`: Reshapes array without copying data

code_walkthroughs.title: Creating and Reshaping an Array
code_walkthroughs.code:
import numpy as np
arr = np.arange(1, 10).reshape(3, 3)
print('Shape:', arr.shape)
print('Diagonal sum:', np.trace(arr))
code_walkthroughs.explanation: Creates a 3x3 matrix containing numbers 1 to 9 and computes the sum of its main diagonal (1 + 5 + 9 = 15).

practice_challenges.title: Matrix Creation & Diagonal Trace
practice_challenges.description: Read an integer `N` from input. Create an `N x N` matrix filled with numbers from `1` to `N*N` (using `np.arange(1, N*N + 1).reshape(N, N)`). Print the sum of its diagonal elements (trace) as an integer.
practice_challenges.starter_code:
import numpy as np

n = int(input())
# Create NxN array and print diagonal sum
practice_challenges.solution_code:
import numpy as np

n = int(input())
arr = np.arange(1, n * n + 1).reshape(n, n)
print(int(np.trace(arr)))

hints.level_1_nudge: Use np.arange(1, n*n + 1).reshape(n, n) to construct the matrix.
hints.level_2_strategy: np.trace(arr) computes the sum of diagonal elements.

lessons.title: Boolean Masking, Fancy Indexing & Broadcasting
lessons.concept_markdown:
- **Boolean Indexing**: Passing a condition `arr[arr > 5]` filters elements matching criteria instantly in compiled C code.
- **Fancy Indexing**: Passing an integer array `arr[[0, 2, 4]]` selects non-contiguous rows or columns.
- **Broadcasting**: NumPy automatically stretches compatible array dimensions during arithmetic without allocating redundant memory copies.

code_walkthroughs.title: Filtering Array with Boolean Masks
code_walkthroughs.code:
import numpy as np
nums = np.array([12, 45, 7, 88, 33, 91])
filtered = nums[nums > 40]
print(filtered)
code_walkthroughs.explanation: `nums > 40` produces a boolean array used directly as an index filter.

practice_challenges.title: Filter Multiples with Boolean Masking
practice_challenges.description: Read a space-separated line of integers from input. Convert them to a NumPy array. Filter and print only the numbers that are divisible by both 3 and 5 (multiples of 15). Print the filtered numbers space-separated, or `'None'` if none match.
practice_challenges.starter_code:
import numpy as np

# Read numbers and filter multiples of 15
practice_challenges.solution_code:
import numpy as np

nums = np.array([int(x) for x in input().split()])
mask = (nums % 3 == 0) & (nums % 5 == 0)
res = nums[mask]
if len(res) > 0:
    print(' '.join(map(str, res)))
else:
    print('None')

hints.level_1_nudge: Combine conditions using the bitwise & operator: (nums % 3 == 0) & (nums % 5 == 0).
hints.level_2_strategy: Apply the mask nums[mask]. If len(res) > 0, join with spaces, else print 'None'.

sessions.title: Session 18 - NumPy Tricks: Conditional Selection & Stats

lessons.title: Vectorized np.where, np.clip & Extrema Indices
lessons.concept_markdown:
- `np.where(condition, x, y)`: Vectorized ternary operator `(if cond then x else y)`.
- `np.clip(arr, a_min, a_max)`: Caps values outside boundary intervals.
- `np.argmax(arr)` / `np.argmin(arr)`: Returns index positions of maximum and minimum elements.
- `np.unique(arr, return_counts=True)`: Finds unique items and their counts.

code_walkthroughs.title: Vectorized Value Replacement with np.where
code_walkthroughs.code:
import numpy as np
scores = np.array([45, 80, 20, 95])
status = np.where(scores >= 50, 'Pass', 'Fail')
print(status)
code_walkthroughs.explanation: `np.where` evaluates element-wise, replacing scores >= 50 with `'Pass'` and others with `'Fail'`.

practice_challenges.title: Clamp and Replace Values
practice_challenges.description: Read a space-separated line of numbers from input. Convert to a NumPy array. Replace any negative values with `0`, and cap any values above `100` to `100`. Print the transformed array elements space-separated.
practice_challenges.starter_code:
import numpy as np

# Clamp numbers to range [0, 100]
practice_challenges.solution_code:
import numpy as np

arr = np.array([int(x) for x in input().split()])
clamped = np.clip(arr, 0, 100)
print(' '.join(map(str, clamped)))

hints.level_1_nudge: Use np.clip(arr, 0, 100) to constrain all array values.
hints.level_2_strategy: Call np.clip(arr, 0, 100) and print elements joined with spaces.

questions.title: Min-Max Feature Normalization
questions.description: Read a space-separated line of floats. Normalize the array using Min-Max scaling: `(x - min) / (max - min)`. If all numbers are identical (`max == min`), return all zeros. Print normalized values rounded to 2 decimal places, space-separated.
questions.starter_code:
import numpy as np

# Implement Min-Max scaling
questions.solution_code:
import numpy as np

arr = np.array([float(x) for x in input().split()])
min_v = np.min(arr)
max_v = np.max(arr)
if max_v == min_v:
    scaled = np.zeros_like(arr)
else:
    scaled = (arr - min_v) / (max_v - min_v)
print(' '.join(f'{x:.2f}' for x in scaled))

hints.level_1_nudge: Find min and max using np.min() and np.max().
hints.level_2_strategy: Compute (arr - min_v) / (max_v - min_v), and format each element as f'{x:.2f}'.
hints.level_3_clue:
scaled = (arr - min_v) / (max_v - min_v)
print(' '.join(f'{x:.2f}' for x in scaled))
